# Border and Opacity Patterns for Event Status

Covers how calendar applications visually distinguish accepted, tentative,
unresponded, and declined events. See [citations.md](../citations.md) for
source details.

## Google Calendar

Google Calendar encodes response status through fill patterns [10]:

| Status | Visual Treatment |
|--------|-----------------|
| Accepted/Attending | Solid color fill |
| Maybe/Tentative | Diagonal lines (hatching) across event |
| Not responded | Outline only (no fill) |
| Declined | Outline with strikethrough text |

Direct quote: "If you're attending an event, the event will be a solid color.
If you've answered maybe to an event, you'll see diagonal lines across it.
If you haven't replied yet, you'll just see the event's outline. If you said
no, you'll only see the outline and the event will be crossed out." [10]

Google does NOT use opacity as a native mechanism for status differentiation.
The encoding is structural: fill, hatching, outline, and text decoration [10].

## Apple Calendar

Apple Calendar uses symbol-based indicators for invitation status [11]:

- Individual invitee responses shown with distinct icons (accepted, maybe,
  declined, available/no response, unavailable/no response) [11]
- Community reports indicate dashed/dotted outline with clear background for
  unaccepted invitations, though this is not confirmed in official Apple
  documentation [11]
- Declined events are hidden by default (View > Show Declined Events) [11]
- In month view: all-day events = color bars, timed events = colored dots [11]

Apple's approach relies more on icons and symbols than on fill/opacity
patterns compared to Google [11].

## Microsoft Outlook

Outlook uses a left-side indicator bar with pattern encoding [8]:

| Status | Left Bar Treatment |
|--------|-------------------|
| Busy | Solid bar in category color |
| Tentative | Hash marks (diagonal lines) on bar |
| Free | White/empty bar |
| Out of Office | Always purple |
| Working Elsewhere | Dotted pattern on bar |

For all-day events, the patterns extend to the full day cell [8]:
- Busy + Category: entire cell shaded in category color
- Tentative: category color with hash-mark pattern
- Working Elsewhere: dotted background

Note: Outlook distinguishes event STATUS (organizer-set: busy/tentative/free/OoO)
from attendee RESPONSE status. The left-bar encoding represents the organizer's
"show as" setting, not the attendee's reply [8].

Users report New Outlook made these indicators "too subtle" [22].

## Fantastical

Fantastical uses dot/circle indicators for availability [12]:

| Status | Indicator |
|--------|-----------|
| Busy | Solid dot |
| Free | Open circle |
| Tentative | Dotted circle |
| Unavailable | Forbidden sign (⊘) |

"Not all calendar services support all statuses" [12].

No documentation found on how Fantastical renders event blocks differently
for tentative vs accepted events [12][28].

## iCalendar Standard (RFC 2445)

The iCalendar specification defines two separate status concepts:

1. **Event STATUS** (organizer-set): TENTATIVE, CONFIRMED, CANCELLED
2. **Attendee PARTSTAT** (per-invitee): ACCEPTED, DECLINED, TENTATIVE, NEEDS-ACTION

Calendar apps may conflate these visually. Google Calendar's encoding [10]
maps to PARTSTAT (attendee response), while Outlook's [8] maps to the "Show As"
property (which correlates with event STATUS).

## Cross-Application Pattern Summary

| Status | Google | Apple | Outlook | Fantastical |
|--------|--------|-------|---------|-------------|
| Accepted | Solid fill | Solid fill (inferred) | Solid left bar | Solid dot |
| Tentative/Maybe | Diagonal hatching | Symbol indicator | Hash marks on left bar | Dotted circle |
| Not responded | Outline only | Dashed outline (community reports) | (varies) | — |
| Declined | Outline + strikethrough | Hidden by default | Removed/faded | — |

## TkInter Canvas Implementation Options

TkInter Canvas does not support CSS-style gradients or true alpha transparency
on shapes. Available options for encoding status:

| Technique | TkInter Method | Suitable For |
|-----------|---------------|-------------|
| Solid fill | `create_rectangle(fill=color)` | Accepted events |
| Dashed border | `create_rectangle(dash=(4,4))` | Tentative/unresponded |
| Stipple pattern | `create_rectangle(stipple='gray50')` | Pseudo-transparency |
| Manual hatching | Loop of `create_line()` calls | Diagonal lines (maybe) |
| Border only (no fill) | `create_rectangle(fill='', outline=color)` | Not responded |
| Strikethrough | `create_line()` across text | Declined |

The `stipple` option provides built-in patterns (gray12, gray25, gray50, gray75)
as dot-based pseudo-transparency, but not diagonal hatching.

For diagonal hatching matching Google Calendar's style, manual line drawing via
`create_line()` in a loop is required. CSS diagonal stripes use
`repeating-linear-gradient(45deg, ...)` [25] — the TkInter equivalent is
explicit line geometry.

## Gaps and Limitations

- Apple Calendar's exact fill/outline behavior for tentative events is not
  confirmed in official documentation — community reports only
- Fantastical's event block rendering (vs dot indicators) is undocumented
- No dark-mode-specific rendering details found for any app's status patterns
- TkInter stipple patterns are coarse and may not look professional at small
  event block sizes
